stories.title: New dwarf planet candidate discovered by NSF–DOE Rubin Observatory
stories.summary: Scientists using the NSF–DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory have identified a large object, provisionally designated ED138, orbiting beyond Pluto. Preliminary analysis suggests it may be one of the largest dwarf planet candidates ever found, potentially joining the five other known dwarf planets if confirmed by follow-up observations.
stories.finding: Scientists using the NSF–DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory have identified a large object, provisionally designated ED138, orbiting beyond Pluto. Preliminary analysis suggests it may be one of the largest dwarf planet candidates ever found, potentially joining the five other known dwarf planets if confirmed by follow-up observations.
stories.significance: If confirmed, ED138 would join the five other known dwarf planets, expanding our understanding of the solar system's composition and the objects residing in its distant regions. The discovery highlights the Rubin Observatory's capability to detect moving objects in crowded star fields.
stories.caveat: The object ED138 is currently a "dwarf planet candidate" and its classification is preliminary. Further observations by other observatories are needed to confirm its nature and status as a dwarf planet.
entities:
NSF
DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory
International Astronomical Union Minor Planet Center

stories.title: NASA’s Perseverance Offers Clues to Protect Crews From Mars Dust
stories.summary: NASA's Perseverance rover measured fine and ultrafine Martian dust particles clinging to spacesuit materials over 1,645 Martian days. The findings, to be published in PNAS, indicate these particles are small enough to penetrate lungs and bloodstream, informing future spacesuit and habitat designs, dust-removal procedures, and crew health standards for Mars missions.
stories.finding: NASA's Perseverance rover measured fine and ultrafine Martian dust particles clinging to spacesuit materials over 1,645 Martian days. The findings, to be published in PNAS, indicate these particles are small enough to penetrate lungs and bloodstream, informing future spacesuit and habitat designs, dust-removal procedures, and crew health standards for Mars missions.
stories.significance: This research provides the first on-site measurements of fine and ultrafine dust particles on Mars, which is crucial for informing spacesuit and habitat design, developing dust-removal procedures, and establishing crew health standards for future human missions to Mars. Understanding how different materials collect dust can guide the selection of protective coatings and materials to mitigate health risks for astronauts.
stories.caveat: The source does not specify material limitations; independent verification is not established.
entities: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

stories.title: Stars brewing in a nebulous cauldron
stories.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope captured detailed images of N159, a star-forming region in the Large Magellanic Cloud, revealing dim stars less than a tenth the Sun's mass and distinguishing young stellar objects from fully evolved stars. This allows researchers to study star formation in conditions similar to the early Universe.
stories.finding: The James Webb Space Telescope captured detailed images of N159, a star-forming region in the Large Magellanic Cloud, revealing dim stars less than a tenth the Sun's mass and distinguishing young stellar objects from fully evolved stars. This allows researchers to study star formation in conditions similar to the early Universe.
stories.significance: This research provides an opportunity to study H II regions under conditions similar to the early Universe, offering insights into star formation processes during that epoch. The ability to observe the entire sequence of star formation in N159 helps astronomers understand the evolution of collapsing molecular clouds.
stories.caveat: Preprint / working paper; peer review is not established. The source does not specify material limitations; independent verification is not established.

inputFacts.title: Stars brewing in a nebulous cauldron
inputFacts.summary: Astronomers, using data from the James Webb Space Telescope's Near-Infrared Camera (NIRCam), detected extremely dim stars less than a tenth as massive as the Sun and distinguished larger, hotter, fully evolved stars from young stellar objects in the N159 star-forming region of the Large Magellanic Cloud. Their results indicate that the western region of N159 has a higher concentration of young stellar objects, suggesting it is in an earlier stage of stellar collapse.

stories.title: Whatcha lookin’ at? Social anxiety heightens brain sensitivity to others’ gaze
stories.summary: A University of Michigan study found that young adults with higher social anxiety showed stronger brain responses (N400) when a person's gaze and a descriptive word didn't match, suggesting heightened neural sensitivity to social cues. However, this sensitivity did not improve their explicit judgments about the gaze's meaning, potentially contributing to increased rumination.
stories.finding: A University of Michigan study found that young adults with higher social anxiety showed stronger brain responses (N400) when a person's gaze and a descriptive word didn't match, suggesting heightened neural sensitivity to social cues. However, this sensitivity did not improve their explicit judgments about the gaze's meaning, potentially contributing to increased rumination.
stories.significance: This research offers a new perspective on social anxiety, suggesting it may not solely be a source of distress but could also involve an enhanced sensitivity to social cues. This sensitivity might have both benefits, such as noticing important signals, and drawbacks, like increased worry, depending on the social context.
stories.caveat: While individuals with higher social anxiety showed greater neural sensitivity to gaze meaning, this advantage did not translate into improved accuracy or speed in later explicit judgments. The study did not establish whether this sensitivity helps people navigate real-world social situations.
stories.localConnection: University of Michigan research in Ann Arbor.

stories.title: They get knocked down—but they get up again
stories.summary: University of Michigan researchers found that low doses of the herbicide dicamba caused oxalis weeds to produce more flowers in the first year of a study. While this did not consistently translate to increased seed production or genetic inheritance of the trait, it altered pollinator visitation patterns, with smaller flowers receiving fewer individual visits.
stories.finding: University of Michigan researchers found that low doses of the herbicide dicamba caused oxalis weeds to produce more flowers in the first year of a study. While this did not consistently translate to increased seed production or genetic inheritance of the trait, it altered pollinator visitation patterns, with smaller flowers receiving fewer individual visits.
stories.significance: This finding suggests that unintended exposure to low doses of herbicides, such as from drift, might inadvertently enhance weed reproduction rather than suppress it. This could have implications for agricultural practices and home lawn care, potentially making weed control more challenging.
stories.caveat: While the study found that oxalis produced more flowers, it did not consistently translate to increased seed production in the second year of the experiment. Additionally, plants with more flowers due to dicamba exposure had lower pollinator visitation rates, and their flowers were smaller. The study also focused on a single weed species, and other species or populations might respond differently.
stories.localConnection: University of Michigan research in Ann Arbor.

inputFacts.title: NASA-funded Study Details One of Oldest Mars Meteorites Ever Found
inputFacts.summary: The rose-colored meteorite Teghaza 001, discovered in the Sahara Desert in 2022, has been identified as a piece of Mars that formed over 4.1 billion years ago. This makes it one of the oldest Martian meteorites ever found on Earth, providing a rare glimpse into Mars' ancient crust and formation, including evidence of water alteration around 4.1 billion years ago.

inputFacts.summary: The composition of a mollusk's microbiome is primarily determined by its species (family tree) rather than its living environment. inputFacts.title: The Land of the Standing-Up Rocks
inputFacts.summary: Approximately 27 million years ago, a volcanic eruption in southeastern Arizona released a massive amount of volcanic material, leading to the collapse of the ground and the formation of the Turkey Creek caldera. inputFacts.title: As concerns over purchasing power dominate, consumer sentiment moves sideways
inputFacts.summary: Consumer sentiment remained largely unchanged in October 2026, with the Consumer Sentiment Index falling to 48.0 from 48.1 in September. This stability masks underlying shifts, as increases in sentiment among Republicans and Democrats were offset by declines among independents. The decline in the Current Conditions subindex was primarily due to an 18% plunge in buying conditions for durable goods, driven by higher interest rates and affordability concerns. Homebuying conditions also plummeted, with 85% of consumers deeming it a bad time to buy a house, largely due to high interest rates.
